graph.title: Golden Staff Guardians (7306)
notes: The four groups the checker reports are real, separate models in this booklet, so I did not connect them. They are (1) the red motorcycle (pp.3-7), (2) the golden-staff temple (pp.8-18), and (3, 4) two mummy minifigures (p.2). Page 19 only shows the finished models side by side, and no step joins one model to another.

The two mummy minifigures' own pieces (heads, torsos, legs, headdresses) are not in the parts list, so they are not nodes. Each mummy holds one khopesh sword and one scarab shield in its hands. Since the hands are not nodes, I joined each mummy's sword and shield with a contact edge (b54-b56 for one, b55-b57 for the other). This pairing is an assumption.
Where a catalogue entry has no port for the join (the fairing's studs, the studs on 3046a, 3040b and 30176, and the stud on the tail-light dynamite), the edge uses a null port.

The steps have no parts boxes, so I assigned pieces to steps from the parts list and the pictures. Exact stud positions (rows and columns on the 4x8 base plate and the 1x6 bricks) are my best reading of the pictures.

The chassis/fairing/wheel joins are approximate. The fairing pegs go into the chassis, and the wheel stub axles go into the chassis fork and the rear axle hole. The catalogue lists only pin-hole.1, pin-hole.2 and axle-hole.1 on the chassis.

The rear carrier (60478) is assumed to sit on the fairing's rear studs. One clip plate (4085c) holds the rifle and the other holds the dynamite. The 6019 clip holds the 60478's handle and carries the trans-red tail light.

The three tan 1x6 bricks are read as follows: A is on row 2 of the base plate, B is beside it on row 1, and C is on top of the two corner bricks. The 3020 plate is joined under the base plate's front-right edge.
The golden staff (b53) is pushed onto the blue jumper's centre stud. The axle plate assembly (b51/b52) is inserted into the black Technic brick's pin hole.
Only one joined edge is given per pair of pieces, using representative ports, even where a plate or brick overlaps several studs.
